records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Before designing a conversion for an engine family, diff an installed flat title against its native/separate VR sibling to isolate VR-specific executables, runtime libraries, data, configuration and extension seams.
records.applicability: Engine families or titles where both flat and VR variants are available; strongest local pairs are Skyrim, Fallout 4 and Borderlands 2.
records.nonApplicability: Does not prove the same binary offsets, code or assets can be reused across games or builds.
constraints: Compare exact builds and architectures.
Attribute each observed difference to the correct title/layer.
Do not copy proprietary binaries or assets.
failureModes: Treating unrelated version drift as a VR change.
Assuming a sibling implementation can be transplanted wholesale.
records.fallback: Use public engine/runtime evidence and title-specific instrumentation when no sibling exists.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Model a separate VR edition as a potentially distinct executable/runtime product rather than assuming the flat executable merely receives a camera hook.
records.applicability: Commercial VR editions such as Borderlands 2 VR, Skyrim VR, Fallout 4 VR and Hellblade VR.
records.nonApplicability: Not appropriate for titles whose VR mode lives inside the same executable/install.
constraints: Record executable architecture and runtime libraries.
Preserve flat and VR identities separately.
failureModes: Underestimating renderer/input/platform changes hidden behind a familiar title name.
records.fallback: Classify as in-place native VR or injected conversion when evidence supports those routes.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Recognise and preserve the single-install native-VR pattern where the same title adds a VR runtime path without a separately branded VR executable.
records.applicability: Installed examples include No Man's Sky and Thumper.
records.nonApplicability: Does not imply the VR path shares every renderer, UI or input behaviour with flat mode.
constraints: Separate common game content from VR runtime/config evidence.
Test mode selection and rollback explicitly.
failureModes: Mistaking an optional runtime DLL for proof that VR is currently functional.
records.fallback: Require a launch/runtime acceptance test before promoting capability.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Separate native VR plumbing from higher interaction parity: use bounded extension/plugin layers for body IK, hands, grabbing, collision, holsters and physics rather than entangling them with the base runtime.
records.applicability: Strongly evidenced by the installed Skyrim VR SKSEVR + VRIK/HIGGS/PLANCK stack and supported by Fallout 4 VR's F4SEVR seam.
records.nonApplicability: Plugin APIs, offsets and licences are title-specific and cannot be assumed portable.
constraints: Attribute each capability to base game, extender or exact plugin.
Keep component versions and licences explicit.
failureModes: Flattening multiple mods into one untraceable capability claim.
Allowing an interaction layer to destabilise locomotion/runtime plumbing.
records.fallback: Retain the native VR baseline with interaction layers disabled independently.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: For flat-game conversion research, inspect the game-root graphics proxy/interception seam, VR loader and title configuration as separate components before modifying engine logic.
records.applicability: The installed Starfield route exposes root dxgi.dll, openxr_loader.dll and dedicated VR config/UI files.
records.nonApplicability: File co-location alone does not identify exact implementation provenance or prove runtime success.
constraints: Keep the flat baseline reversible.
Bind findings to exact game/tool builds.
Treat proxy/loaders as privileged compatibility surfaces.
failureModes: Conflating runtime loading with correct stereo/camera behaviour.
records.fallback: Use an external or engine-specific adapter route if root interception is unavailable or unsafe.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Put headset runtime, display, tracking and controller-device choices behind explicit adapters and data-driven bindings where the engine permits it.
records.applicability: Installed Cyberpunk vorpX, VRChat, GORN and Hellblade VR expose multiple runtime/device integration surfaces.
records.nonApplicability: Does not imply every title can switch runtimes without title-specific compatibility work.
constraints: Keep runtime selection explicit.
Version bindings with the title/runtime.
Do not treat vendor-specific plugins as standards.
failureModes: Hard-wiring one headset path into core game logic.
Mixing tracking and rendering backend state invisibly.
records.fallback: Provide one proven runtime plus a clearly isolated alternate adapter.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Structure difficult flat-to-VR conversions as a common VR/interception framework plus a narrow title adapter and title-specific correction configuration.
records.applicability: The installed RDR2 R.E.A.L. VR topology exposes RealVR64 framework, RDR2 ASI adapter, graphics/input/API interception and title configuration as distinct pieces.
records.nonApplicability: The proprietary R.E.A.L. VR implementation is analysis-only; this teaches architecture, not code reuse.
constraints: Preserve framework/title boundaries.
Keep proprietary implementation out of the corpus.
Pin game build compatibility.
failureModes: Building one giant title-specific patch with no reusable framework seam.
Treating creator framework metadata as independent proof.
records.fallback: Use a standards-based independent framework with a separately authored title adapter.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Model temporal reconstruction/stereo correction as its own conversion layer, separate from head pose and runtime transport.
records.applicability: Starfield config exposes DLSS/AER and Nvidia DLSS/TAA repair controls; RDR2 config exposes stereo TAA repair, render mode and yaw prediction controls.
records.nonApplicability: Specific algorithms/settings are title/build-specific and should not be copied blindly.
constraints: Measure per-eye coherence and frame timing.
Keep repair toggles reversible and independently testable.
failureModes: Calling a route 'VR-ready' when pose works but temporal history diverges between eyes.
Masking artefacts with unrelated comfort changes.
records.fallback: Disable the unstable temporal feature or use a lower-complexity stereo path for diagnosis.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Treat world scale, HUD geometry/distance, dominant eye, camera recentering, FOV and head-follow behaviour as separate calibration dimensions.
records.applicability: Installed Starfield and RDR2 conversion configs expose these dimensions independently.
records.nonApplicability: Values from one title or headset are not universal defaults.
constraints: Keep seated and standing calibration distinct when needed.
Record operator/headset acceptance separately from config presence.
failureModes: Using one global scale/FOV knob to compensate for unrelated UI or camera faults.
records.fallback: Return to neutral scale and calibrate one spatial dimension at a time.

records.licenceBoundary: Mixed proprietary/open corpus. Reuse only independently authored methods and specifically licensed open components; never copy game/mod binaries, assets, proprietary profiles or restricted implementation.
records.reusableMethod: Externalise VR actions and controller-family bindings as versioned data where practical so device support can evolve without rewriting title logic.
records.applicability: VRChat, GORN and the installed Cyberpunk vorpX package expose action/binding files for multiple controllers/runtimes.
records.nonApplicability: Game actions still require title-specific semantic adapters.
constraints: Keep action semantics stable across device mappings.
Test handedness and fallback controls explicitly.
failureModes: Embedding controller-specific button assumptions throughout gameplay code.
Changing action semantics when adding a new device.
records.fallback: Use a canonical action layer with one proven mapping and add devices incrementally.
